profile.edit.title: Edit profile
profile.nickname.help: Shown instead of your callsign. Leave blank to use the callsign.
profile.avatar.unreadable: That picture could not be read. Try a JPEG or PNG.
profile.callsign.licensed.help: Leave blank unless a radio authority issued you one.
profile.callsign.licensed.unusual: That is an unusual shape for an issued callsign. Saved as typed.
profile.nsec.warning: Anyone with this key controls this identity. Back it up somewhere safe and never share it.
profile.nsec.invalid: Invalid nsec — must be a bech32 nsec1… string
profile.nsec.no_npub: Could not derive npub from nsec
profile.licence.does.title: What this does
profile.licence.does.body: Everything this device sends will go out as {name} instead of {derived}, and a signed identity announcement will bind {name} to the key you already have. Your key does not change, and neither does {derived}.
profile.licence.proves.title: What it proves, and what it does not
profile.licence.proves.body: The announcement proves that whoever holds this key wrote these packets. It proves nothing about your entitlement to the callsign: an {derived} name is checked against its key by arithmetic, an issued callsign has no arithmetic relationship to any key, and XPRS has no register and issues no credentials. Another station can announce the same callsign with a different key and both announcements will verify. Anyone who wants certainty checks your administration's own licence register, out of band, once. This app never transmits an opinion about whether a callsign is licensed.
profile.licence.station.title: Others will see you as a station
profile.licence.station.body: A callsign is read as a person only when it begins X1. A licensed callsign says nothing about whether its holder is a person or a mast, and guessing would be worse than saying station, so you will appear in the Stations list rather than in People.
profile.licence.mail.title: Mail already on its way
profile.licence.mail.body: Peers keep reaching you under both names. But mail a neighbour was already carrying for your old callsign may not be handed over; ask the sender to resend. Apps you already have open keep the old name until you reopen them.
profile.licence.amateur: On amateur bands a licensed callsign is the only one that may be transmitted at all, and encryption is not permitted there.
profile.encryption.desc.off: Encrypt everything this profile stores on this device. Enabling deletes the profile's current data and starts fresh.
profile.encryption.desc.device: Everything this profile stores on this device is encrypted, and unlocks automatically on this device. Add a password to protect it even from someone holding the unlocked phone.
profile.encryption.desc.password: Everything this profile stores on this device is encrypted. Unlocked by your password mixed with the secret key.
profile.encryption.enable.title: Encrypt this profile
profile.encryption.enable.body:
All existing data of this profile on this device will be DELETED (messages, chat history, media). The profile starts fresh, fully encrypted.

It unlocks with your fingerprint (or the phone's screen lock). You can add a password afterwards.
profile.encryption.enabled: Profile encrypted. Restart XPRS to complete.
profile.encryption.remove.title: Remove encryption
profile.encryption.remove.body_device: The encrypted data on this device will be DELETED and the profile returns to unencrypted storage, fresh. Anything written from then on sits on the disk in the clear.
profile.encryption.remove.body_password: Enter the profile password. The encrypted data on this device will be DELETED; the profile returns to unencrypted storage, fresh.
profile.encryption.removed: Encryption removed. Restart XPRS to complete.
profile.encryption.no_nsec: Profile has no nsec — cannot enable encryption
profile.password.label: Password
profile.password.add.title: Add a password
profile.password.add.warning: Your data stays intact. From now on the profile needs this password (emoji welcome) — the device key is dropped, and there is NO recovery if you forget it.
profile.password.remove.title: Remove password
profile.password.remove.body: Enter the current password. The profile stays encrypted, but it will unlock with your fingerprint alone.
profile.password.change.title: Change password
profile.password.new.title: New password
profile.password.new.warning: Your data stays intact — only the password changes. No recovery if you forget it.
profile.lock.title: Lock profile
profile.lock.body: XPRS will close to lock the profile. Background message reception stops until you unlock it again.
profile.backup.need_storage: Storage access is needed to save the backup.
profile.backup.grant_storage: Grant storage access to keep a copy that survives uninstalling the app.
profile.backup.passphrase.title: Backup passphrase
profile.backup.passphrase.shared: The backup is kept in shared storage, so it is always encrypted. Leave blank to keep no backup. If you forget the passphrase, the backup cannot be restored: there is no recovery.
profile.backup.passphrase.optional: Encrypt the backup with a passphrase. Leave blank for a plaintext backup. If you forget it, the backup cannot be restored — there is no recovery.
profile.backup.note.shared: The backup is encrypted with your passphrase. Without one, no backup is kept.
profile.backup.note.plaintext: A plaintext backup holds your secret key in the clear — anyone with access to this phone's storage can read it. Add a passphrase to encrypt it.
profile.callsigns.title: Callsigns
profile.callsigns.help: Your key's own callsign is the base and never changes. Add the callsign each authority issued you, one per country you operate in, and choose which goes on the air. A conversation keeps the callsign it began under.
profile.callsigns.base: Derived from your key — always yours
profile.callsigns.pinned.one: {n} conversation keeps another of your callsigns.
profile.callsigns.pinned.other: {n} conversations keep another of your callsigns.
